prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with neck and back strain after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 9 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1458; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Nearly all findings rest on the patient's own pain reports; imaging and exam tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Two similar charges on the same day are being checked.
text: Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain. The reported mechanism is consistent with the injuries described, and the patient has no known prior injury to the cervical or lumbar regions. Over the course of nine visits, care consisted of spinal mobilization, soft tissue therapy, home stretching instruction, and graded activity. The treatment followed a typical course, with visit frequency reduced as symptoms improved and the patient was discharged to self-directed exercise. Most of the clinical picture rests on the patient's own pain reports, as cervical and lumbar range of motion, neurological screening, and orthopedic provocation tests were unremarkable, and cervical and lumbar imaging obtained at intake showed no acute abnormality. Two similar treatment charges recorded on the same date of service are under review for billing accuracy. Prognosis is good with continued home exercise.
